findings.evidence: `ScalarAut.smul_tmul`, `isGroupLikeElem_smul`, `val_smul` are stated for `{K L A}` `[CommSemiring K] [CommSemiring L] [Algebra K L] [Bialgebra K A]` (TauCeti/Algebra/Bialgebra/GroupLike/ScalarAut.lean:35-37, 66, 97); `Continuous.lean:107,139` likewise quantify over `{A : Type v} [Semiring A] [Bialgebra k A]`. `baseChangeMap` itself is general in `k`, `K` (CommHopfAlgCat/BaseChange.lean:48,59). No general commutation lemma exists in TauCeti/Algebra/TensorProduct/BaseChange.lean.
findings.fix: Add the general lemma to `TauCeti/Algebra/Bialgebra/GroupLike/ScalarAut.lean` (or `TauCeti/Algebra/TensorProduct/BaseChange.lean`) for `{K L A B}` with `[CommSemiring K] [CommSemiring L] [Algebra K L]`, `f : A →ₐc[K] B`, `σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L`: `Bialgebra.TensorProduct.map (BialgHom.id L L) f (σ • x) = σ • (Bialgebra.TensorProduct.map (BialgHom.id L L) f x)`, plus its `GroupLike.map` corollary, and derive `baseChangeMap_smul`/`geometricCharacterMap_smul` from it.
findings.issue: `baseChangeMap_smul` proves a fully generic fact (base change of a map commutes with the scalar-factor action) only for `L = AlgebraicClosure k` and only for `CommHopfAlgCat.{u} k` morphisms; the induction uses nothing but `ScalarAut.smul_tmul` and `baseChangeMap_apply_tmul`, both of which hold for any `L/K` and any bialgebra hom. Consequently `geometricCharacterMap_smul` is only available for the absolute Galois group, whereas the surrounding modules state their analogues generically.

findings.evidence: TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Torus/CharacterLattice/Basic.lean:57-69 already proves both `Module.Free ℤ` and `Module.Finite ℤ` for the torus character lattice, and TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Torus/Cocharacter.lean:54-89 consumes exactly those (`let _ := characterLattice_module_free_of_torus ...`), as does MultiplicativeType/GaloisModule.lean:91-95 (`Module.Finite ℤ`).
findings.fix: State `galoisLatticeProperty k M := (Module.Free ℤ M ∧ Module.Finite ℤ M) ∧ ∀ x : M, IsOpen {σ | M.ρ σ x = x}`; discharge membership with the existing `characterLattice_module_free_of_torus`/`characterLattice_module_finite_of_torus`, and derive the rank-`n` equivalence downstream when a basis is needed.
findings.issue: `galoisLatticeProperty` defines the objects of `GaloisLatticeCat` by `∃ n, Nonempty (M ≃+ (Fin n →₀ ℤ))` rather than the standard `Module.Free ℤ M ∧ Module.Finite ℤ M`. This coordinate form gives consumers of the new category no `Module.Free`/`Module.Finite` instances, no connection to `Basis`/`finrank`, and it is what forces the `let _ : Module ℤ X := X.hV2` gymnastics and the hand-built `eAdd : Y ≃+ X` in the `IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms` proof (lines 66-75).

summary: Two level problems: the scalar-action commutation lemma is proved only in the algebraic-closure/bundled-category special case although its whole neighbourhood is stated for arbitrary L/K and arbitrary bialgebras, and the defining property of the new GaloisLatticeCat states finite freeness in an ad-hoc coordinate form instead of Mathlib's Module.Free/Module.Finite.
